chats.lastText:
*ROOTED: ANCHORED IN TRUTH*

Day 3
*Rooted in Love When Identity Is Attacked*
Identity attacks are common today. Labels are assigned quickly. Worth is often tied to performance, popularity, or approval. Paul prays that believers would be rooted and grounded in love—because love secures identity when pressure comes.

When you’re not rooted in God’s love, criticism feels crushing. Failure feels defining. Approval becomes addictive. But when love is your foundation, you don’t crumble under rejection or inflate under praise.

_[16] that He would grant you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with might through His Spirit in the inner man, [17] that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; that you, being rooted and grounded in love,_
*—Ephesians 3:16-17 (NKJV)*

Christ dwelling in you changes how you see yourself. Love reminds you that you are not your mistakes, your past, or your productivity. You are His.

_[1] There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit._
*—Romans 8:1 (NKJV)*

REFLECTION:
Do you believe God loves you—or are you still trying to earn it?

PRACTICAL STEP:
Write down one lie you’ve believed about yourself. Replace it with a truth from Scripture.

PRAYER:
Father, let Your love go deeper than my insecurities. Secure my identity in You. Amen.

Day 3
*Rooted in Love When Identity Is Attacked*
Identity attacks are common today. Labels are assigned quickly. Worth is often tied to performance, popularity, or approval. Paul prays that believers would be rooted and grounded in love—because love secures identity when pressure comes.

When you’re not rooted in God’s love, criticism feels crushing. Failure feels defining. Approval becomes addictive. But when love is your foundation, you don’t crumble under rejection or inflate under praise.

_[16] that He would grant you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with might through His Spirit in the inner man, [17] that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; that you, being rooted and grounded in love,_
*—Ephesians 3:16-17 (NKJV)*

Christ dwelling in you changes how you see yourself. Love reminds you that you are not your mistakes, your past, or your productivity. You are His.

_[1] There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit._
*—Romans 8:1 (NKJV)*

REFLECTION:
Do you believe God loves you—or are you still trying to earn it?

PRACTICAL STEP:
Write down one lie you’ve believed about yourself. Replace it with a truth from Scripture.

PRAYER:
Father, let Your love go deeper than my insecurities. Secure my identity in You. Amen.

WHEN THE LORD IS MY SHEPHERD 
When the Lord Is Your Shepherd, You Have Enough

Do not measure how well you are doing by what you have stored away—money in the bank, possessions in the house, plans secured for tomorrow..

Scripture gives us a deeper kind of security:

“The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.” — Psalm 23:1

Spurgeon understood the secret. Our greatest provision is not what we possess; it is the One Who ho possesses us.

You may not have everything you hoped for. You may not know how tomorrow will unfold. There may be needs you cannot yet see a way to meet.

But if the Lord is your Shepherd, you are not abandoned.

He knows what you need.

He knows where He is leading you.

He knows when to make you lie down, when to lead you beside still waters, and when to walk with you through the valley.

So don't let an uncertain bank balance produce a certain fear.

Your Father is not limited by your resources.

Thank God for what He has provided. Work faithfully with what He has placed in your hands. Plan wisely. Be responsible. But don't confuse your provision with your Provider.

Your security is not ultimately in what is in your account.

It is in the Shepherd who never leaves His sheep.

And if you have Him, you have the greatest treasure heaven could give.

_A Testimony of God's Wisdom_⭐

*THE WISDOM OF GOD HAS ASTONISHED ME*

_There Is None Like Our God (His Omniscience, Omnipotence, and Omnipresence)_

The wisdom of God has completely astonished me. The more I walk with Him, the more I realize that no human mind can compare with His infinite knowledge, understanding, and wisdom. He is the Mighty Warrior, the Lord of hosts, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. His wisdom is not learned—it is eternal, perfect, and supernatural.
The Scriptures declare:
_Daniel 2:20–22_
_"Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and might are His... He reveals deep and secret things; He knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with Him."_
Likewise, Job 37:16 asks:
_"Do you know the wondrous works of Him who is perfect in knowledge?"_

These words have become a living reality to me. I have witnessed the Lord reveal things that no human being could have known. Through dreams, night visions, and His gentle whisper, He has graciously warned me, exposed the enemy's schemes, and reminded me that nothing is hidden from His sight. This has continually strengthened my confidence that our God is all-knowing and all-wise.
As the Lord Himself declares:
_Isaiah 46:9–10_
_"I am God, and there is no other... declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things that are not yet done, saying, 'My counsel shall stand, and I will do all My pleasure.'"_

Who else can reveal tomorrow before it arrives? Who else can expose what is hidden in darkness before it unfolds? Even the plans of the enemy are never beyond God's knowledge. Before Satan devises a scheme, God already knows its outcome. Before a word reaches our lips, He already knows it. Truly, His understanding is beyond measure.
The Bible also reminds us:
_Proverbs 15:3_
_"The eyes of the LORD are in every place, keeping watch on the evil and the good."_
Nothing escapes His attention. Nothing surprises Him. He neither sleeps nor slumbers. His perfect knowledge governs heaven and earth.

Many times during prayer, the Lord encouraging me with promises of His mighty works. He has already assured me of the assignments awaiting me: performing wonders and miracles, healing the lame, causing the deaf to hear, healing all kinds of sicknesses, raising the dead, shutting even the skies, and doing what has never been done by anyone in this world. I came to know this not through my own understanding, but by His might and by the Spirit of the Lord. He has spoken peace to my heart and assured me that He is able to do wonders beyond human imagination. Like the prophets and apostles before us, I believe that our God is still the God of miracles. Nothing is impossible with Him, and He is able to accomplish whatever He purposes according to His perfect will.

As I behold His creation, I am left speechless. The heavens proclaim His glory, the earth displays His craftsmanship, and the entire universe silently testifies that there is an incomparable Designer behind it all. Every star, every mountain, and every living creature declares that our God is infinitely wise.
As Psalm 92:5 proclaims:
_"How great are Your works, O LORD! Your thoughts are very deep."_
The more I seek to understand Him, the more I discover that His greatness is beyond human comprehension. I have simply resolved to let God be God. No one can compete with Him, question His wisdom, or overturn His purposes.
The apostle Paul expressed this truth beautifully:
_Romans 11:33–36_
_"Oh, the depth of the riches both of the wisdom and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are His judgments and His ways past finding out!... For of Him and through Him and to Him are all things, to whom be glory forever. Amen."_

Indeed, God has turned the wisdom of this world into foolishness, just as Paul also wrote in 1 Corinthians 1:25:
_"Because the foolishness of God is wiser than men, and the weakness of God is stronger than men."_
Therefore, let us humble ourselves before the Almighty. Instead of trusting in human wisdom, let us seek the wisdom that comes from above. The God who declares the end from the beginning is faithful. His counsel will stand forever, His purposes cannot fail, and His wisdom remains beyond comparison.

Brethren, I have reached one conclusion: there is no one like our God. To Him alone belong all wisdom, knowledge, understanding, power, majesty, and glory forever. Amen.

We can find a common ground of peace through the Holy Spirit. The apostle Paul said that “the kingdom of God is…righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit” (Romans 14:17). You have to be in a relationship with God before you can be in peace with others. When you are at peace with God, you can be at peace with others. The Bible talks about God’s presence reigning in peace through our lives. If you want the power of God in your life, maintain your relationships through the bond of peace.
Rom.14.17 - For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit,

Whenever this meets you, Pray.

The day maybe almost over, Before you close your eyes tonight, ask yourself honestly:

Did I truly have no time to pray—or did I simply fail to make prayer a priority?

We often say, “I was too busy.” But we found time to scroll, talk, eat, work, watch, plan, and worry. Prayer is rarely defeated by a completely empty schedule; it is often displaced by things we considered more urgent.

So start making room.

Pray before you pick up your phone in the morning. Give God the first moments of your attention.

Turn waiting time into prayer. While commuting, walking, cooking, or waiting for an appointment, talk to God.

Pray in short moments throughout the day. You don't need an hour every time. Five intentional minutes are better than repeatedly postponing prayer.

Put prayer on your schedule. If you schedule meetings because they matter, schedule prayer because eternity matters more.

Use ordinary activities as prayer reminders. Every meal, doorway, alarm, or routine task can become a prompt to pray.

End the day with God, not merely with your screen. Before sleep, thank Him, confess your sins, commit tomorrow to Him, and pray for others.

And remember: you don't find time for prayer—you make time for prayer.

The issue is not always that the day is too full.

Sometimes our priorities are.

 “Pray without ceasing.” — 1 Thessalonians 5:17

Before this day ends, don't merely regret that you didn't pray.

Stop. Get alone with God. And pray.

‎
‎
‎
‎ *THE BATTLES OF FLESH*
‎
‎_Overcome fleshly desires with the Spirit's power_
‎
‎The flesh has desires that are contrary to the Spirit. It calls out for attention, pulling us in directions that lead away from God’s will. But as Christians, we must decide whether we will listen to the cries of the flesh or focus on the voice of the Spirit. The Apostle Paul understood this struggle deeply. He said, _“I beat my body and make it my slave, so that after I have preached to others, I myself will not be disqualified for the prize” (1 Corinthians 9:27)._ This is a powerful reminder that we must actively discipline ourselves to stay in control.
‎
‎As Christians, we face many temptations. Without self-control, it’s easy to fall into the desires of the flesh immorality, jealousy, drunkenness, and all forms of wickedness. Paul writes in Galatians 5:17, “For the flesh desires what is contrary to the Spirit, and the Spirit what is contrary to the flesh.” When we give in to the flesh, we defame the image of Christ we are meant to reflect. It is shameful to profess Christ with our lips while allowing our flesh to win the battle in our lives.
‎
‎The works of the flesh are clear, as described in _Galatians 5:19-21: “The acts of the flesh are obvious: sexual immorality, impurity and debauchery; idolatry and witchcraft; hatred, discord, jealousy, fits of rage, selfish ambition, dissensions, factions and envy; drunkenness, orgies, and the like._” These actions tear us away from God and tarnish our testimony.
‎
‎However, there is hope. We are not left to fight this battle alone. By feeding the Spirit, we can overcome the desires of the flesh. This can be done through daily study of God’s Word, constant prayer, and allowing the Spirit to guide us. As we grow in our relationship with God, His strength equips us to resist the flesh’s temptations. _“So I say, walk by the Spirit, and you will not gratify the desires of the flesh” (Galatians 5:16)._
‎
‎It is crucial that we discipline ourselves in the same way Paul did, and allow the Spirit to take the lead. Let us strive to feed our spirits so that we may grow stronger, overcome our sinful desires, and reflect Christ more fully in our lives.
‎

Remember this today:

God never asked you to be strong enough for everything. He never expected you to hold every burden, fix every problem, or carry every weight on your own. His Word reminds us in 2 Corinthians 12:9 that His power is made perfect in our weakness—not in our perfection, not in our performance, not in our strength... but in the very places where we feel tired, overwhelmed, or unsure.

If you feel worn out, you’re not failing—you’re actually standing in the very place where His grace works best. When you come to the end of yourself, you’re not at the end of hope; you’re at the beginning of His strength.

Let God meet you there.
Let Him lift what you can’t.
Let Him be the strength you don’t have today.

You were never meant to carry everything alone. You were meant to lean on the One who never grows weary, who never changes, and who never stops caring for you. Trust Him with what feels heavy. Surrender what feels impossible. His grace is enough, and His strength will carry you through. 🤍🙏🏻

PREPARE FOR COSTLY INTERNET, couretsy of MP Marianne Kitany :

Among the proposals are:

1. Introduction of an internet metre number to facilitate billing subscribers based on consumption.

2. Moving away from unlimited internet packages towards consumption-based billing, similar to how electricity or water is billed.

3. Increased monitoring of internet usage by Internet Service Providers.

These proposals deserve serious public scrutiny because affordable internet is no longer a luxury. It is essential infrastructure.

Making internet access more expensive could have consequences far beyond social media:

1. Businesses — higher operating costs and reduced digital activity.

2. Schools and students — increased costs for online learning and digital resources.

3. Workers and jobs — businesses under financial pressure may cut staff or reduce operations.

4. Communication — families, communities and businesses would have to spend more simply to stay connected.

5.Access to information — millions of Kenyans could be priced out of the digital public square.

And the timing matters.

As Kenya approaches another election cycle, we must ask: Who benefits when accessing information becomes increasingly expensive?

.teach Bible books that talk about blessings

In a small town nestled between rolling hills, there lived a woman named Sarah. She was known for her kindness and unwavering faith. Every day, she would gather the local children to tell them stories from the Bible, emphasizing the blessings that came from living a good life. The children loved these tales, eagerly awaiting each new lesson.

One sunny afternoon, Sarah decided to focus on the Book of Deuteronomy. She explained how Moses conveyed God’s promises of blessings for obedience to His commandments. The children listened intently as she described how these blessings included prosperity, health, and peace in their homes. Inspired by the stories, they began to discuss what it meant to live a blessed life.

As days turned into weeks, Sarah introduced them to the Book of Psalms. She shared passages that spoke of joy and gratitude, emphasizing that blessings often stemmed from having a thankful heart. The children started practicing gratitude in their daily lives, thanking God for simple pleasures like food and friendship.

The climax of their journey came when they reached the Book of Matthew. In this book, Sarah highlighted Jesus’ teachings about blessings found in being humble and merciful. The children were captivated by the Beatitudes—their eyes wide with wonder as they learned that true happiness comes from serving others and seeking justice.

With their newfound understanding of blessings through these biblical texts, the children decided to put their lessons into action. They organized a community service project, helping elderly neighbors with chores and sharing food with those in need. As they worked together, laughter filled the air, and they experienced firsthand the joy that comes from giving.

In the following weeks, word spread throughout the town about the children's efforts. More families joined in, creating a ripple effect of kindness that transformed their community. People began to appreciate not only material blessings but also the warmth of fellowship and support.

As winter approached and holiday decorations adorned homes across town, Sarah gathered everyone once more for a celebration of gratitude. They reflected on their journey through Scripture and acknowledged how embracing these teachings had brought them closer together while fostering an atmosphere rich in love and generosity.

In conclusion, Sarah smiled at her lively group of young learners. The stories from Deuteronomy, Psalms, and Matthew had not just been words; they had become a way of life for many in their small town. Through understanding biblical blessings—both spiritual and practical—the children discovered that true happiness is often found in connection with others and living out one’s faith through action.
